scope: One-paragraph educational field notes. The sentences are habitat-search guidance or source-reported synthesis, not a habitat suitability model, preference study, confirmed new locality, or rarity-tier input.
displayRule: One paragraph per species; insert field cue before trailing DENR status where present.

records.fieldCue: Shaded canopy gaps and streamside trees offer concealed hunting perches for this baza.
During seasonal movements, wooded ridgelines and openings along forest margins can bring passing Grey-faced Buzzards into view.
Pied Harriers search low over wet grassland, marsh margins and fallow fields.
Reedbeds, flooded grassland and marsh edges provide hunting space for Eastern Marsh Harriers quartering over wetland vegetation.
Open fields with isolated trees and poles provide hunting perches for Black-winged Kites, which also hover while searching for prey.
Along estuaries, Brahminy Kites patrol mangrove margins, tidal flats and channels, taking food from the water and exposed shoreline.
Large, slow-moving rivers and wetlands with tall bankside trees provide perches overlooking the water for Grey-headed Fish Eagles.
Coastal inlets, sheltered bays and broad river mouths combine open hunting water with elevated perches used by White-bellied Sea Eagles.
Shaded forest tracks and small canopy openings provide glimpses into the mid-storey where this goshawk hunts from cover.
Wooded slopes and openings in the upper forest canopy offer views of Rufous-bellied Eagles moving above the trees.
Changeable Hawk-Eagles soar above wooded hills and forest margins and hunt from concealed tree perches.
Lowland and lower-montane forest, including mature wooded slopes and some selectively disturbed stands, form the main setting for Pinsker's Hawk-Eagle.
Wooded ridge crests and canopy openings provide broad views of Crested Honey Buzzards during seasonal movements.
The Philippine Honey Buzzard uses wooded landscapes, including upper-canopy perches and gaps between tree crowns.
On Mindanao, Philippine Eagle nesting landscapes include large emergent trees above wooded slopes and ravines in lowland and upper hill forest.
Philippine Serpent Eagles use forest edges, wooded foothills and riparian corridors, where their calls carry across canopy openings.
Narrow gaps in wooded hillsides and forest margins offer brief views of Japanese Sparrowhawks during passage.
During migration, Chinese Sparrowhawks may appear over wooded valleys and forest margins.
Within shaded forest, the Besra may perch in the mid-canopy before flying through narrow gaps between trees.
Over reservoirs, river reaches and coastal shallows, Ospreys search open water and dive to seize fish.
Shallow marshes and seasonally flooded grasslands offer open water and vegetated edges used by Northern Pintails.
Philippine Ducks use inland and coastal wetlands, including small ponds, tidal creeks and larger open-water areas.
Sheltered wetland backwaters and flooded vegetation may provide feeding and resting areas for Eastern Spot-billed Ducks.
Wandering Whistling Ducks gather on freshwater marshes and lakes, often among patches of emergent vegetation.
Spotted Whistling Ducks use tree-bordered wetlands and freshwater marshes, with historical Philippine observations also extending to coastal marsh.
Forested mountain streams provide wet rock surfaces and nearby vegetation that may shelter McGregor's Slender Stream Toad.
Shaded stream corridors with boulders and shallow riffles may provide refuge and activity sites for Müller's Slender Stream Toad.
Western Mindanao Toadlets have been observed on sapling and shrub leaves near streams, including moderately disturbed forest edges.
Low ferns and shrub leaves form recorded perches for the Eastern Mindanao Toadlet in montane forest.
Marine Toads often occupy disturbed lowland areas, including yards, drainage edges and temporary pools that fill after rain.
Within limestone forest, shaded leaf litter and sheltered rock crevices may provide moist refuges for Walter's Limestone Forest Frog.
The forest floor is a documented habitat of the Masked Wrinkled Ground Frog, including terrestrial sites away from immediate stream margins.
Broad leaves and low branches in humid forest may offer sheltered perches for Günther's Wrinkled Tree Frog.
The Mindanao Variable Forest Frog has been recorded on the floor of mature forest at Mount Hilong-Hilong.
Shaded ground cover and deep leaf litter in terrestrial forest may shelter Jagor's Variable Forest Frog.
In northeastern Mindanao, fallen wood and leaf litter may create sheltered spaces for this broad-headed forest frog.
Cloudy montane forest provides a cool, damp setting for Navjot Sodhi's Cloud Frog, with shaded vegetation offering possible activity sites after rain.
Rabor's Horned Tree Frog calls high in the forest canopy and has also been recorded on vegetation in Mindanao surveys.
Asian Mangrove Frogs may occupy shallow pools and muddy backwaters along mangrove margins, including brackish edges.
Rice paddies, irrigation channels, still pools beside streams and swampy forest patches are documented habitats of the Philippine Field Frog.
Large pools, wetland margins and flooded cultivated ground provide potential shallow-water habitat for the East Asian Bullfrog.
White-spined Fanged Frogs have been recorded beside rocky mountain streams, including riparian sites above 900 m.
Fallen logs, rocks, stream margins and the adjoining forest floor provide shelter and activity sites for the Philippine Swamp Frog.
Mindanao Fanged Frogs occupy small, shallow forest streams and nearby banks, ground surfaces and low vegetation.
Shaded stream margins and damp ground in riparian forest may provide activity sites for the Western Mindanao Fanged Frog.
Streams through lowland and lower-montane forest are reported habitats of the Philippine Guardian Frog.
The Visayan Fanged Frog may use saturated ground and shallow edges of forest streams within its island range.
Small puddles and shallow standing water may provide activity sites for this tiny aquatic frog during wet periods.
Common Puddle Frogs occupy shallow water and muddy margins, including small pools and waterlogged ground along lowland tracks.
In villages and gardens, damp leaf litter, planted beds and sheltered ground cover can support the small terrestrial Greenhouse Frog.
Philippine Crocodiles inhabit freshwater marsh channels, vegetated pond margins and calmer river reaches, where basking and shelter sites occur near water.
Saltwater Crocodiles move through tidal channels, estuarine banks and mangrove creeks and can travel far into freshwater river reaches.
Sunlit branches, forest-edge saplings and adjoining shrub vegetation may offer perches for the Philippine Bloodsucker.
In northeastern Mindanao, Two-spotted Flying Lizards have been recorded on trunks near forest edges and adjoining coconut groves (Sanguila et al., 2016).

records.fieldCue: Northeastern Mindanao records place Chartreuse-spotted Flying Lizards on coconut palms and exposed trunks adjoining forest (Sanguila et al., 2016).

records.fieldCue: Near Malagos, Mindanao, Günther's Flying Lizards used trees in secondary forest and coconut palms beside the forest (McGuire & Alcala, 2000).
Daytime observations place Mindanao Flying Lizards on trunks several metres above ground in primary and mature secondary rainforest (Sanguila et al., 2016).
Ornate Flying Lizards have been recorded on trunks in primary and secondary forest and coconut stands close to wooded areas (Sanguila et al., 2016).
Brightly lit coconut palms and exposed tree trunks are documented perches for Reticulated Flying Lizards in plantation landscapes.
At Agusan Marsh, Anglehead Lizards have been recorded in peat-swamp forest, where shaded trunks and nearby vegetation provide potential perches.
Streams and rivers offer escape water and raised bankside perches for Philippine Sailfin Lizards, including branches and exposed trunks.
Asian Vine Snakes use slender branches, vines and shrubs along wooded edges, where their narrow green bodies blend with foliage.
Intertwined branches and lower-canopy vegetation may provide nighttime activity sites for the Philippine Blunt-headed Cat Snake.
Tree limbs and dense climbing vegetation may offer nighttime hunting routes for the Dog-toothed Cat Snake.
Mangrove branches and creekside trees above tidal water offer sheltered climbing habitat for the Mangrove Snake.
In shaded forest, slender branches and hanging vegetation may provide nighttime perches for the White-spotted Cat Snake.
Philippine Reed Snakes have been recorded in soil and beneath forest-floor debris, moving through sheltered ground.
In northeastern Leyte, Variable Reed Snakes have been recorded among riparian boulders and leaf litter in dipterocarp forest.
Paradise Flying Snakes move between tree crowns by day, using trunks and connected canopy branches.
Fallen wood, ground cover and vegetated forest edges may provide retreat and movement sites for the Philippine Red-tailed Ratsnake.
The sunlit shrub layer and lower trees around forest openings may provide activity sites for Maren's Bronzeback Snake.
Philippine Bronzeback Snakes may move through shrubs and connected branches around forest gaps.
Fine branches, suspended vines and dense shrubs offer likely climbing routes for the Philippine Whip Snake.
Trees and climbing plants at wooded edges create connected aboveground pathways for the Red-tailed Green Ratsnake.
Common Wolf Snakes use sheltered ground, rock crevices and modified lowland surroundings, including areas near houses.
Philippine Brown Deer browse shoots and foliage in forest clearings and adjoining grassland, often moving along sheltered vegetated paths.
On the forest floor, rooted soil, wallows and disturbed leaf litter may reveal movements of Philippine Warty Pigs.
Fruiting trees and connecting branches in woodland provide likely nighttime feeding and movement routes for the Philippine Palm Civet.
Malay Civets travel along ground-level routes through secondary woodland, cultivated edges and other vegetated mosaics.
Small Asian Sheath-tailed Bats roost in caves and partly lit rock cavities, including recorded sites on Siargao and in the Agusan region.
Bare-rumped Sheath-tailed Bats shelter in hollow trees, rock cracks and buildings and emerge after dusk to forage over nearby landscapes.
Black-bearded Tomb Bats shelter in cave recesses and narrow rock crevices, sometimes gathering in maternity groups.
Caves and karst may provide daytime shelter for Philippine Tailless Roundleaf Bats, with adjoining forest and waterways offering possible flight corridors.
In forested karst country, cave chambers may provide daytime roosts for Philippine Dusky Roundleaf Bats.
Fawn-colored Roundleaf Bats have been recorded in caves on Siargao and in Agusan del Sur, where sheltered chambers provide roosting space.
Large Mindanao Roundleaf Bats are reported from forested karst landscapes, where sheltered cave spaces may be used for roosting.
Diadem Roundleaf Bats have documented cave roosts on Mindanao and Siargao amid wooded landscapes.
Philippine Forest Roundleaf Bats occur from lowland to montane forest on Mindanao, with records reaching about 1,100 m elevation.
Large hollow trees, including dao, provide recorded shelters for Lesser Asian False-vampires, which also roost in caves and buildings.
Little Long-fingered Bats shelter by day in caves, tunnels and abandoned mines before moving through nearby airspace after dusk.
Caves within forested karst may provide roosting spaces for Great Long-fingered Bats, with wooded corridors forming possible flight routes.
Philippine records include Lesser Naked Bats roosting in hollow trees and coconut palms, with occasional cave use.
Wrinkle-lipped Free-tailed Bats form colonies in caves and can also occupy rock crevices and buildings.
Openings above wooded waterways and cultivated land may provide flight corridors for Sulawesian Free-tailed Bats.
A Luzon GPS study found most recorded foraging locations of Golden-capped Flying Foxes in closed forest, with roosting trees occurring across a wider landscape (de Jong et al., 2013).

records.fieldCue: High-elevation mossy forest on Mount Kitanglad is a documented habitat of the Mindanao Pygmy Fruit Bat.
Fruiting and flowering vegetation provides food for Lesser Short-nosed Fruit Bats, while leaves, trees and buildings offer daytime roosts.
Fruiting trees in the forest canopy may provide feeding opportunities for the White-winged Flying Fox.
Philippine Large-headed Fruit Bats may forage among fruiting trees and connected upper-canopy vegetation in forest.
Flowering forest plants provide nectar-feeding opportunities for the Philippine Dawn Bat during nighttime activity.

styleNote: Habitat detail written as flowing, declarative natural-history prose. Inferences remain qualified without repetitive disclaimers.
